PullRequest.Title: Send the Copilot billable owner to the TAS assignments endpoint
PullRequest.Body:
sends `github_core_copilotbillableentityid` to the TAS assignments endpoint, from the optional `billable_owner` field in the `copilot_internal/user` response (who pays for the user's Copilot), next to the org and enterprise ids.

if the response doesn't have it nothing changes, and a malformed value is ignored. github.com only returns it when its flag is on for the user, so there's no client flag. a change in only this value is picked up on the next assignments refresh, same as the enterprise ids.

tests in `assignmentFilters.spec.ts` and `copilotToken.spec.ts`. core is in a separate PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot authentication and token refresh for a signed-in GitHub user
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold, forced, or near-expiry token request, the existing token endpoint request and copilot_internal/user request run in parallel and both must complete before ExtendedTokenInfo is returned. The diff only copies billable_owner from the already-fetched user response and adds a constant-time getter; it adds no critical-path boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mint a Copilot token from the GitHub token
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One token request per cold, forced, or near-expiry authentication attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same token request ran with the same Promise.all placement and cardinality before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with user-info retrieval; both existing requests must settle before authentication advances.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One user-info request per cold, forced, or near-expiry signed-in authentication attempt, with existing fetcher fallback/retry behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The full user-info response was already fetched and parsed once per authentication attempt for plan, quota, and organization metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already on the authentication critical path and parallel with token minting; the diff reads one additional bounded account identifier from its existing parsed response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One billable_owner object per authenticated user/token. The expected universal key is a single short identifier, not a collection, so work does not scale with organizations, files, requests, or workspace size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two existing network requests are issued by one Promise.all per authentication attempt. Warm valid-token reads use the cached token and perform neither request. The diff does not alter concurrency, retries, or coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A valid Copilot token is reused until forced or within five minutes of expiry. The new field is retained with that existing token and incurs no work on warm reads beyond two property reads when filters are requested; misses and retry behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path shows the user-info boundary and Promise.all predate the changed assignment, while the changed code performs only a shallow reference copy and constant-time validation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact endpoint latency and refresh frequency vary, but neither network-call count nor response parsing cardinality changes. The added retained bytes are one expected short identifier per token.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no boundary or retry is added, and the added CPU/allocation/retention is bounded to one small metadata object per cached token.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial and periodic TAS assignment refresh using Copilot account filters
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing TAS client obtains filters and serializes them into its assignments request during initial fetch and later refreshes. The changed getter contributes one optional short string to the existing filter map; it does not initiate a refresh or add a request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST filters to the existing TAS assignments endpoint
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing assignments request per TAS client initial/periodic or account-triggered refresh; the new filter adds at most one value to each payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same assignments request already serialized and sent the other Copilot account filters on each refresh; the payload lacked this one identifier.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The assignments request is required for treatment refresh, but the diff changes only its bounded payload metadata and does not increase request cardinality or move the request onto a new path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One optional universal key per assignments request. Effective cardinality is one value per user, independent of workspace size, treatment count, organization count, and history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Delegate initial fetch, hourly refresh, and user-info-triggered refresh behavior are unchanged. Existing delegate replacement revokes and disposes superseded delegates. The diff adds no loop, queue, Promise, or concurrent request source.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The TAS delegate uses its existing memento/client cache and refresh schedule. Filters read the current cached Copilot token on each request; absent or malformed billable owner values produce undefined. The diff creates no new cache key, negative-cache retry, or invalidation path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line only inserts a value into an existing map, while endpoint creation, refresh timer, user-change trigger, and delegate lifecycle are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The upstream TAS client's exact polling internals are external, but repository code establishes that this line is a filter provider for an already-configured boundary. Even at repeated refreshes, the incremental serialization and network bytes are constant and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: request frequency and concurrency are unchanged, and the incremental serialization/network cost is a bounded single identifier.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced authentication/token caching and TAS assignment refresh boundaries, including cold/warm behavior, cardinality, concurrency, and lifecycle. The PR adds one bounded metadata field to already-existing fetch and assignments flows; it introduces no actionable performance regression and does not itself fix a proven shipped performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
